2020 Annual Report to Stockholders

About the Company
Acadia is a leading provider of behavioral healthcare services across the United States. Acadia
operates a network of 227 behavioral healthcare facilities with approximately 9,900 beds in 40 states
and Puerto Rico. With more than 20,000 employees serving approximately 70,000 patients daily, Acadia
is the largest stand-alone behavioral health company in the U.S. Acadia provides behavioral healthcare
services to its patients in a variety of settings, including inpatient psychiatric hospitals, specialty
treatment facilities, residential treatment centers and outpatient clinics.

My Fellow Stockholders
We are pleased to share our solid financial and operating performance for 2020, in what was an extraordinary and
challenging year for Acadia Healthcare, the nation, and the entire world since the onset of the COVID-19 global pandemic.
We faced these challenges with the same determination and resilience that has supported our business and our mission
since Acadia’s inception. More than ever, we are mindful of our critical role as a leading provider of behavioral healthcare
services. The ongoing uncertainties and economic and societal concerns have resulted in strong demand for our services,
especially for those already struggling with mental health and substance use issues and the added fear and isolation caused
by the pandemic.

2020 Accomplishments Set the Stage for Future Growth
At the end of 2020, we reached an agreement to sell the entirety of Acadia’s U.K. operations to Waterland Private Equity, and
we were pleased to complete the sale in January 2021. This was a significant milestone for Acadia, as it enables us to focus
singularly on our U.S. operations and strengthens our financial flexibility to pursue our strategic agenda. We are committed
to our efforts to extend Acadia’s market reach and enhance our service offerings in the U.S., which will in turn maximize
long-term value for our stockholders.
Our U.S. operations performed well in 2020. At the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, we took immediate steps to respond to
the crisis and implemented recommended precautionary measures and safety protocols throughout our operations. Our
top priority has always been and continues to be the health and safety of our staff, patients, and visitors. As restrictions were
put in place that limited physical contact with providers, we quickly expanded our telehealth capabilities to better reach and
support our patients. Additionally, we launched a national behavioral health crisis hotline designed to offer urgent assistance
to anyone across the country in need of mental health or substance use treatment services.
While our volumes declined in the early phase of the pandemic when many stay-at-home orders were implemented across
the U.S., we experienced greater patient admissions across all our service lines once restrictions eased. Reflecting these
demand trends, we achieved $2.1 billion in revenue from continuing operations in 2020, compared

While our volumes declined in the early phase of the pandemic when many stay-at-home orders were implemented across
the U.S., we experienced greater patient admissions across all our service lines once restrictions eased. Reflecting these
demand trends, we achieved $2.1 billion in revenue from continuing operations in 2020, compared with $2.0 billion in 2019.
Our same facility revenue from continuing operations increased 3.9 percent for 2020, reflecting a 1.4 percent improvement in
patient days and a 2.5 percent increase in revenue per patient day.
During 2020, we made strategic investments in our future growth in the U.S., expanding our market reach through bed
expansions and additional service offerings. For the year, we added 240 beds to existing facilities, added 220 beds through
the opening of two joint venture facilities, and opened six comprehensive treatment centers (CTCs) in the U.S.
We extended our strong track record of partnering with leading health systems and hospitals across the country. In
December, we opened Ascension St. Thomas Behavioral Health, a new 76-bed inpatient facility, through our joint venture with
Ascension St. Thomas in Nashville, Tennessee.
We also announced the formation of a joint venture with Henry Ford Health System, one of Michigan’s premier academic and
integrated health systems, to address the growing, unmet need for accessible, high-quality behavioral health services in the
Detroit area. The new hospital, expected to open in late 2022, will have 192 beds with the potential to expand to meet future
demand for inpatient services in the area. In addition to offering a full continuum of inpatient care, the hospital will also
serve as a destination academic site for the training of inpatient psychiatry residents, medical students, nurses, and other
healthcare professionals.
As we continue to work with these valuable partners, we can make a positive difference in the lives of more individuals and
families throughout the respective regions.

Following the closing of the U.K. sale, on January 29, 2021, the Company sent notices of redemption for $650 million
of 5.265% Senior Notes due 2023 and $390 million of 6.500% Senior Notes due 2024 to the holders of such notes. The
redemption of this $1,040 million of additional debt was completed in March and was funded with cash from the balance
sheet of $430 million and proceeds from a new five-year $1,025 million senior secured credit facility.
Together, the sale of the U.K. business, our cost management initiatives and our disciplined capital allocation strategy have
put us in a strong financial position for 2021 and beyond.
Diverse Service Lines Are Key Different i at or
Without question, 2020 was a challenging and difficult year, and even more pronounced for those already struggling with mental
health and substance use issues. While there are reasons to be optimistic about the diminishing impact of COVID-19 on our
lives with the increased availability of an effective vaccine and a gradual return to more normal societal routines, we anticipate
the demand for behavioral health services will continue to increase post-pandemic. Studies have shown the prolonged
isolation, economic uncertainties, higher unemployment and grief related to the loss of lives over the past year have led to
increased anxiety and depression and a corresponding rise in substance use. We are also seeing higher demand as societal
acceptance of behavioral health increases and coverage options for those seeking treatment continue to expand and improve.
As we look to 2021, we believe Acadia is well positioned to address the needs of those seeking treatment with our four diversified
service lines offering exceptional, high levels of care for our patients. Our expansive network of treatment facilities and options
enable greater access to care, allowing us to serve the diverse needs

look to 2021, we believe Acadia is well positioned to address the needs of those seeking treatment with our four diversified
service lines offering exceptional, high levels of care for our patients. Our expansive network of treatment facilities and options
enable greater access to care, allowing us to serve the diverse needs of all our patients with the appropriate level of care.
Our acute care business is our largest service line, representing approximately 47% of U.S. revenue in 2020. This segment
provides the highest level of care. We have a strong network to support this service line, with 44 inpatient acute psychiatric
facilities across 20 states and Puerto Rico, and we see opportunities to further grow our share of this highly fragmented market.
Our specialty business is focused on inpatient residential programs that treat patients who are suffering from either
substance use or eating disorders. This area of treatment is highly specialized, and Acadia is further differentiated by our
strong marketing platform and national clinical referral network.
Our comprehensive treatment centers (CTCs) operate on an outpatient basis and combine behavioral therapy and medication
to treat substance use disorders. Studies indicate the pandemic has caused a resurgence in opioid use and a higher risk
for overdoses in the wake of widespread unemployment, isolation, and disruption in treatment delivery during lockdowns.
With 131 clinics, Acadia is the largest provider of medication-assisted treatment in the U.S. Additionally, we continue to see
positive legislative support for our services and favorable reimbursement trends, including expanded funding of Medicare
and Medicaid in 2020.
Acadia also operates residential treatment centers (RTCs), that provide longer-term residential treatment for children and
adolescents with behavioral health disorders in a non-hospital setting. Acadia’s RTC business is differentiated by our unique,
specialized programs led by strong facility management teams and our relationships with state-referring agencies.
As we continue to deal with the lingering effects of the COVID-19 pandemic and other societal and economic disruptions, we
believe each of these service lines will be critical to our success in meeting the needs of the patients who seek our care.

Strategy for the Future with Four Pathways to Growth
With our singular focus on our U.S. operations and increased financial flexibility, we intend to make strategic investments in
four distinct areas that will support sustained, long-term growth across our service lines.
(cid:81) First, we believe facility expansions provide us with the best return for our investment. We continue to identify opportunities
to add beds to existing Acadia facilities, which allows us to leverage the respective facilities’ cost structure and improve
operating margins. In 2021, we plan to add approximately 300 beds to meet the growing demand in our current markets.
(cid:81) Our second pathway to growth is joint venture partnerships with health systems across the country to build new
facilities. This strategy provides Acadia with access to attractive markets otherwise inaccessible through acquisitions.
We also benefit from the partner hospital’s established market presence and favorable reputation in the community.
Importantly, joint ventures enable us to integrate physical and mental health services to develop quality programs that
support the local communities.
II

Through our partnership with Covenant Health, we expect to open a new 90-bed inpatient facility in Knoxville, Tennessee, later this year. Looking ahead, we have a solid pipeline of approximately 30 joint venture projects in different
stages, providing significant opportunities to extend our market reach. We expect 2022 to be the strongest year for joint
ventures with our partners to date, with four to five facilities expected to open.
(cid:81) We are also focused on identifying markets throughout the country that are underserved with a shortage of beds for
behavioral health treatment. We believe there are as many as 100 of these market opportunities where Acadia can address this critical need by opening wholly owned de novo facilities.
In 2021, we expect to open one acute inpatient 80-bed facility in Cincinnati, Ohio. Looking to 2023 through 2025, we
expect to open three to four new inpatient facilities annually, including joint ventures and wholly owned de novos. We
also believe there is tremendous unmet demand for medication-assisted treatment in the 32 states where

we expect to open one acute inpatient 80-bed facility in Cincinnati, Ohio. Looking to 2023 through 2025, we
expect to open three to four new inpatient facilities annually, including joint ventures and wholly owned de novos. We
also believe there is tremendous unmet demand for medication-assisted treatment in the 32 states where we currently
operate, and we are looking at target markets for de novos in five additional states. We plan to open 11 CTC locations
throughout the U.S. in 2021, with a goal to open an additional six to ten CTC locations per year from 2022 to 2025.
(cid:81) The fourth pathway to growth for Acadia is through M&A activity. Earlier this year, we announced that we signed a definitive agreement to acquire Vallejo Behavioral, a 61-bed acute facility located in Vallejo, California, from Adventist
Health. Tuck-in acquisitions such as Vallejo have been an important part of Acadia’s growth strategy, and this facility
will be a prominent addition to our portfolio. We believe the fragmented behavioral healthcare industry provides ample
prospects for future acquisitions, and we are well positioned to capitalize on these opportunities.
Our marketing platform is a key differentiator for Acadia that supports these opportunities for growth with a strong,
diversified referral base across all service lines and regions. We work hard to eliminate any barriers to treatment through our
attention to prompt response times from initial outreach to admission. We have an exceptional marketing team who plays an
essential role in the execution of our growth strategy by supporting our facilities and working to reach the many patients that
need our services.
Another important area of focus for Acadia going forward will be within the area of telehealth. We saw the tremendous benefit
of this platform during the early stages of the pandemic, and we believe telehealth provides a unique opportunity to expand
the continuum of care for our patients and still maintain our strong quality proposition.
The utilization of our telehealth platforms will help broaden community outreach, assist with physician coverage, support
increased opportunities for group therapy and encourage more timely assessments. We will continue to evaluate

The utilization of our telehealth platforms will help broaden community outreach, assist with physician coverage, support
increased opportunities for group therapy and encourage more timely assessments. We will continue to evaluate
opportunities to expand our telehealth capabilities through additional support for existing services, expansion of existing
services, and growth into new services.
Positioned for Success as Leading Pure-Play Behavioral Health Company
We are extremely proud of our accomplishments during this difficult year, which again demonstrated that Acadia is setting
the standard for excellence in the treatment of behavioral health and substance use disorders. Our ability to execute our
strategy under extraordinary conditions confirms our strong value proposition, and we are confident we have created a solid
foundation for continued success.
Above all, we are focused on fostering high levels of quality and safety for all our patients and their families. With our
singular strategic focus on our U.S. operations and a strong financial position to support our growth initiatives, Acadia is
well positioned to meet the expected demand for mental health and substance use treatment, with over 20,000 dedicated
employees and experienced clinical teams who support Acadia’s mission. We also benefit from the outstanding leadership of
our senior management team and Board of Directors who are committed to operational excellence and a growth strategy that
delivers value to all our stakeholders.
Together, we look forward to the opportunities before us to deliver the highest quality of patient care, while also extending our
market reach and advancing our market position as a leading pure-play behavioral healthcare provider.
Thank you for the support your investment provides.
Sincerely,
